Walk me through the daily bank reconciliation job L204DF2: what does it produce, and how do check records get from the daily register to the bank files?

Engineering Onboarding Specialist

ENGINEERING ONBOARDING SPECIALIST Completed 1 step Here's a complete walkthrough of job L204DF2, the daily bank reconciliation job. Per the JCL narrative, its stated purpose is: "This daily job prints the daily batch register and bank files." What L204DF2 Produces The job produces these key output files : L204DF2.md Table Output File Description Format ... LAK2LDXP.L204DF.RECON.ACC2528.DTL Reconciliation detail for Account 2528 (Bank Type O) 80-byte FB ... LAK2LDXP.L204DF.RECON.ACC2536.DTL Reconciliation detail for Account 2536 (Bank Type B) 80-byte FB ... LAK2LDXP.L204DF.RECON.ACC0987.DTL Reconciliation detail for Account 0987 (Bank Type T) 80-byte FB ... LAK2LDXP.L204DF.RECON.ACC0499.DTL Reconciliation detail for Account 0499 (Bank Type E) 80-byte FB ... LAK2LDXP.L204DF.RECNBKP2.DTL(+1) Consolidated recon posting tape (all 4 accounts merged) 80-byte FB ... LAK2LDXP.L204DF.BNKFLDTE.DTL(+1) Date-enriched bank records 88-byte FB ... LAK2LDXP.L2BPBNK1.CHECKS.ISSUED.DTL(+1) Checks Issued Detail — deduplicated check issuance records 39-byte FB ... LAK2LDXP.L204DF.ERROR.DISK.DTL Unmatched/error records from bank matching 133-byte FBA ... LAK2LDXP.L204DF.ERROR.FICHE.DTL Error records formatted for microfiche 133-byte FBA ... LAK2LDXP.L204DF.RECNBKP2.DLY.BCKUP(+1) Permanent daily backup of consolidated recon 80-byte FB ... View more How Check Records Flow from the Daily Register to the Bank Files This is the core data path within the job — the "checks issued" pipeline : L204DF2.md Step 1 — Stage the source (SORTA) The Big Record Detail file (LAK2LDXP.L204DF.BIGREC.DTL) — which is the daily register — is copied byte-for-byte (80-byte records) into a temporary Reconciliation Work File (&&RECONCIL). Step 2 — Filter for old/legacy accounts (BNKFLMOD) Program BNKFLMOD reads &&RECONCIL and extracts records belonging to old or legacy bank accounts, writing them to OLDACCT.BNKREC.DTL. Step 3 — Date enrichment (BNKFLDTE) Program BNKFLDTE reads OLDACCT.BNKREC.DTL plus the DATECARD control card, appends 8 bytes of date information to each record (80 → 88 bytes), and writes a new GDG generation of BNKFLDTE.DTL(+1) to tape. Step 4 — Classify into four bank categories (UIBNKDAT) Program UIBNKDAT re-reads OLDACCT.BNKREC.DTL with DATECARD and splits records into four streams based on account/bank type: &&BANKO → Account 2528 &&BANKB → Account 2536 &&BANKT → Account 0987 &&BANKE → Account 0499 Step 5 — Sort into permanent bank files (SORTO/SORTB/SORTT/SORTE) Each temp stream is sorted ascending on positions 1–20 and written to its permanent account reconciliation file (e.g., RECON.ACC2528.DTL). Step 6 — Consolidate to tape (REPRO4) All four account files are merged sequentially (2528 → 2536 → 0987 → 0499) into the consolidated RECNBKP2.DTL(+1) tape with 120-day retention. The Checks-Issued Side Path In parallel with the bank-file classification above, a separate pipeline builds the Checks Issued Detail : L204DF2.md BUILDOUT — Program BUILDOUT reads the same source BIGREC.DTL and transforms each 80-byte record into a compact, standardised 39-byte check-issuance record → temp file &&OUTSTD. SORTD — The 39-byte records are sorted ascending by their entire content, and exact duplicates are eliminated (SUM FIELDS=NONE). The deduplicated output is written as a new GDG generation: L2BPBNK1.CHECKS.ISSUED.DTL(+1). Bank-Match Validation (Error Path) A third path validates specific accounts against a reference file : L204DF2.md SORT1 — Filters &&RECONCIL for records where positions 71–80 equal '0001273518' or '0001273507'. BNKFLBLD — Matches those records against the BANKMTCH VSAM cluster; unmatched/error records go to ERROR.DISK.DTL (133-byte FBA for microfiche printing). REPRO8 — Copies the error file to microfiche tape (30-day retention), conditional on REPRO6 succeeding. Key Operational Notes Restart criticality: 9 (high) — restart from PREPARE if SORTA needs re-running. L204DF2.txt All main-path steps are conditional on RC=0 from all prior steps; any failure skips downstream processing to prevent incomplete data. The four individual account backup steps (BACKUP1–4) run unconditionally, so a point-in-time snapshot is always available even if later steps fail. The spoiled-check file (L201DB.SPOILCHK.DTL) is deleted only on full success, confirming those records have been reconciled. Source: This describes the complete flow within job L204DF2 as documented in L204DF2.md and the JCL source L204DF2.txt (Daily CA-7 space). Upstream jobs that produce BIGREC.DTL and PAYREC.DTL, and downstream consumers of the Checks Issued or account reconciliation files, are not covered in this single job's documentation. When a new-hire crossmatch hit comes in, under what conditions does LOOPS update the claimant's return-to-work date, and where is that date stored?

Engineering Onboarding Specialist

ENGINEERING ONBOARDING SPECIALIST Completed 1 step Based on the documented logic in program UIMB0147 (the New Hire crossmatch letter-generation and RTW-update batch program), here's a comprehensive answer. UIMB0147.md Where Is the Return-to-Work Date Stored? The return-to-work date lives in two places, depending on the source type: Table Storage Location Field Name Format ... LOOPS IMS database — Basic Claim Segment (Segment 1 / LOOPLE01) DB01-DATE-RETURN-WORK Internal packed numeric (F6) ... DB2 claim table TNPV_CLAIM DTE_RETURN_WORK YYYY-MM-DD (DB2 date) ... View more For letter-eligibility processing, the program retrieves the RTW date from TNPV_CLAIM (for T3/TRA sources) or reads it directly from the IMS DB01 segment, then works with it internally as DB01-DATE-RETURN-WORK. A null placeholder of 0001-01-01 (DB2) or 0 (internal) means "no RTW date on file." UIMB0147.md When the RTW date is actually updated, it is written back to the IMS basic claim segment (DB01) via the RTW update process 2300-UPDTE-RTW-DB01. UIMB0147.md Conditions Under Which LOOPS Updates the RTW Date The RTW update logic (paragraph 2300-UPDTE-RTW-DB01 in UIMB0147) uses a decision tree with five outcomes. The RTW date is set to the Date of Hire (HM-DATE-HIRE) from the crossmatch record when — and only when — all of the following hold: ✅ Conditions that trigger an update No existing RTW date on the claim — DB01-DATE-RETURN-WORK = 0. If a non-zero RTW date already exists, the update process exits immediately without changing anything. The saved Date of Hire is non-zero — HM-DATE-HIRE-SAVE ≠ 0. A zero hire date (missing data) prevents the update. One of these additional-claim scenarios is true: (a) No DB10 additional-claim segments exist for the claimant → RTW is set to Date of Hire directly. (b) DB10 segments exist but contain no valid Date of Addition (the indicator field DB10-FILLER-CHK-10 is blank in all segments) → RTW is set to Date of Hire. (c) A valid Additional Claim Date is found AND the Date of Hire ≥ that Additional Claim Date → RTW is set to Date of Hire. ❌ Conditions that prevent the update RTW date already exists (non-zero) → skip entirely, no change. Hire Date is zero → skip, no change. Hire Date < Additional Claim Date → The claimant filed an additional claim after being hired, creating a conflict. RTW is not updated; instead, the record is written to the "RTW Not Updated" exception report (with SSN, Program Code, Date of Claim, Employer FEIN, Date of Hire, Benefit Week Begin, Employer Name, Additional Claim Date, and Separation Code). UIMB0147.md Summary Decision Flow Is RTW date already on claim (DB01-DATE-RETURN-WORK > 0)? └─ YES → STOP. No update. └─ NO → Read DB10 segments for Additional Claim Date ├─ No DB10 segments found → UPDATE RTW = Date of Hire ├─ DB10 found, no valid Date of Addition → UPDATE RTW = Date of Hire ├─ Date of Hire ≥ Additional Claim Date → UPDATE RTW = Date of Hire └─ Date of Hire < Additional Claim Date → DO NOT UPDATE; write exception report Important Context This logic applies specifically to the batch letter-generation step (program UIMB0147, which runs as part of the New Hire crossmatch daily job stream). It describes when the batch program itself writes the hire date into the RTW field. Other CICS-online programs or adjudicator actions may also set the RTW date on a claim through separate paths not documented in this program. The "existing RTW date" comparison that controls letter decisions (e.g., "suppress letters when RTW = Hire Date" or "employer-only letter when Hire Date > RTW") happens before the update logic runs — so the letter decision uses the pre-existing value, and the update logic writes the new value afterward. UIMB0147.md The downstream payment program (UIMB0031) also reads DB01-DATE-RETURN-WORK and sets the return-to-work indicator (DB02-R-W-IND) on payment segments: 0 = no RTW date, 1 = RTW date exists.
